Hi Claire —

Quick technical note on burst behavior and autoscaling:

- Cold starts: our runtime keeps a warm pool of model workers when burst is expected — for short bursts (10-15 minutes) we can route to warm standby and avoid model load cold starts. For very large scale-ups (beyond warm pool), initial token latency can spike while we spin up additional kernels (this typically takes ~45-90 seconds depending on GPU type).
- Recommendation for your marketing spike to ~600 concurrent:
   - Keep 2 GPUs in warm-standby above the reserved capacity and pre-warm additional 4 GPUs 5-10 minutes before the expected spike. We can schedule a pre-warm via an API call or use TrafficPredict to auto-prewarm if you feed expected windows.
   - Autoscaling policy: target CPU/GPU utilization thresholds with rapid scale-out (scale step +2 GPUs) and conservative scale-in (cooldown 10 min) to avoid thrash.
- Cost: rough estimate for the trial month — 4 reserved A100s + warm standby + potential 6 GPU-hour burst (assuming 2 short spikes) ~ $18k–$22k (ballpark). We'll produce a more detailed cost sheet after we confirm expected spike durations.

I'll attach a short runbook for pre-warm and an example autoscaling policy. We can also set up proactive alerts to notify your ops when we pre-warm.

—Vivek
